subject.title: PR1/6 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt, narrow, or reject the proposed shared residual durable-runtime boundary before routable RFC documentation and follow-on implementation are accepted?
rationale: The patch accurately labels itself as provisional, but selecting a new shared persistence and recovery boundary is product and architecture policy that source review cannot settle.

options.title: Require explicit sponsorship first
options.body: Keep the RFC unmerged until a relevant owner explicitly sponsors, narrows, or rejects the shared-boundary direction.

options.title: Accept the residual boundary
options.body: Merge the RFC as a clearly provisional design anchor and review future implementation only within the approved owner-first scope.

options.title: Reject shared durable core
options.body: Close the proposal and require each remaining cross-owner concern to use existing owner-specific APIs instead.

recommendation.title: Require explicit sponsorship first
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC unmerged until a relevant owner explicitly sponsors, narrows, or rejects the shared-boundary direction.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline places this reviewer in the prior discussion, though current-main ownership evidence is incomplete.
